definitions.explanation: To demolish an old or damaged building and construct a new one in its place.

definitions.gloss: to reorganize; to restore; to get back on track
definitions.explanation: To rebuild something abstract such as a business, relationship, health, or life after a setback. Often written as 立て直す for this figurative sense.

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}い{家|いえ}を{建|た}て{直|なお}す。
{地震|じしん}で{壊|こわ}れた{学校|がっこう}を{建|た}て{直|なお}す{計画|けいかく}がある。
examples.english: There are plans to rebuild the school that was destroyed in the earthquake.

examples.japanese: {祖父|そふ}の{代|だい}に{建|た}て{直|なお}したこの{家|いえ}は、もう{築|ちく}{五十|ごじゅう}{年|ねん}になる。
examples.english: This house, rebuilt in my grandfather's generation, is now fifty years old.

examples.japanese: {経営|けいえい}を{建|た}て{直|なお}す。
{体調|たいちょう}を{建|た}て{直|なお}してから{復帰|ふっき}する。
examples.english: I'll return after getting my health back on track.

examples.japanese: {赤字|あかじ}が{続|つづ}いていたが、{新|あたら}しい{社長|しゃちょう}のもとで{会社|かいしゃ}を{建|た}て{直|なお}すことができた。
examples.english: The company had been running deficits, but under the new president they managed to turn it around.

notes:
COMMON PATTERNS:
Godan verb (す ending, conjugates as s-row: {建|た}て{直|なお}さない, {建|た}て{直|なお}します). Transitive — takes a direct object marked with を.

WRITING:
Sense 1 (physical rebuilding) uses {建|た}て{直|なお}す. Sense 2 (figurative rebuilding) is often written {立|た}て{直|なお}す, though the two are sometimes used interchangeably.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {家|いえ}を{建|た}て{直|なお}す (to rebuild a house)
- {経営|けいえい}を{建|た}て{直|なお}す (to restructure a business)
- {体調|たいちょう}を{建|た}て{直|なお}す (to restore one's health)
- {生活|せいかつ}を{建|た}て{直|なお}す (to get one's life back together)
